steps.title: Open Pair
steps.body: Our next strategy is called the Open Pair. When exactly two cells in a unit share the same two candidates, no other cells in that unit can share those candidates. Let's take a look!

steps.title: Spot the Pair
steps.body: In this box, two cells share candidates 3 and 8 — an Open Pair.

steps.title: Why it Works
steps.body: Logically, one of these two cells must be 3 and the other must be 8. If we placed a 3 on the top cell, the other must be 8. If we placed a 8 on the top cell, the other must be 3. That means the 3 and 8 can't be anywhere else in the box!

steps.title: First Open Pair
steps.body: Here's where selecting multiple empty cells comes in! We are going to select the evidence of our strategy. First, select one of the two cells with candidates 3 and 8, then select the other.

steps.title: What Happened?
steps.body: Did you see the effect of the Open Pair? The 3 and 8 candidates were removed from the other cells in this box. Do you notice anything about the remaining cells?

steps.title: Another Open Pair
steps.body: Those last two cells created another Open Pair in this column with the 1 and 9! Let's give those a tap too!

steps.title: Resolved Moves
steps.body: Nice job! Keep in mind that if your selected cells aren't having an effect, they likely aren't a valid strategy or the strategy has no effect on the puzzle!

steps.title: Complete the puzzle
steps.body: Use the Open Pair strategy to complete the rest of this puzzle. We will auto-complete Singles so you can focus on the Open Pairs!

steps.title: Open Triple
steps.body: An Open Triple is three cells in the same unit that collectively contain exactly three candidates between them. Those candidates can't appear anywhere else in the unit.

steps.title: Find the Triple
steps.body: In the bottom-left box, three cells share candidates 1, 4, and 8. They form our Open Triple.

steps.title: Who Gets Eliminated?
steps.body: Because these three cells must take 1, 4, and 8, the rest of the box can't use those digits. Watch the other cells in this box.

steps.title: Apply the Open Triple
steps.body: Tap the three highlighted cells to mark them as the evidence for an Open Triple. We'll clear 1, 4, and 8 from the remaining candidates in this box.

steps.title: What Changed?
steps.body: Nice! Those other cells lost candidates 1, 4, and 8. Keep looking for situations where three cells box out three candidates.

steps.title: Finish the Puzzle
steps.body: Use Open Triples (and the remaining singles) to wrap this up. Singles will auto-complete as they appear.
